title: The promises SECURITY.md makes are true where a driven exploit says they are not
description: Six sentences in SECURITY.md that a driven exploit contradicted on 2026-09-12. The red-team drove each one in a temp directory from the file:line it names; none touched a real secret or this repo. Part 7 of the 3.0 analysis puts these first and the operator's answer to question 1 made the ledger's chain binding rather than advisory: nothing else ships ahead of them.
desiredOutcome: Every SECURITY.md sentence a driven exploit contradicted either holds, or the document says plainly what it does not promise. The evidence ledger's rows carry the journal's chain, so the FAIL-to-PASS rewrite that verify() called clean becomes a finding with a non-zero exit; MCP tool calls reach the guards that already refuse the same operation by another name; a manifest shard rewritten by sed is refused for a subagent as its Edit already is; and a tracked journal file that is gone turns verify red rather than reporting a clean chain over the files that remain.

tasks.title: The evidence ledger carries the journal's chain
tasks.description: Evidence rows get the journal's `prev`/`hash` chain. The functions exist in `_journal_io`; `_evidence_io.append_row` writes a row with neither today, and `grep -c 'sha256|"hash"|"prev"|genesis'` over the two files is the measurement. Driven before the fix: two rows, a plain string replace of FAIL to PASS, then `verify()` returns ok with no findings. The record of the MEASUREMENT - the thing a green gate points at - is the one file with no chain. Done means that rewrite is a FINDING with a non-zero exit, and the clean case still verifies.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__evidence_io.py: a FAIL rewritten to PASS in a recorded row is a finding and exits non-zero; an untouched ledger still verifies clean

tasks.title: MCP calls reach the guards, bound to the operation not the server
tasks.description: `mcp__.*` reaches the four guards, with a branch that resolves the operation rather than the server's name. A filesystem MCP server can today read a dotenv, mark a task done, or turn the journal off in the config with no ask, no deny and no row. The read half was measured as TWO independent failures - the hooks.json matcher launches nothing for an MCP tool name, AND the decision falls through to allow for an unhandled tool - so fixing either alone leaves the hole open. Bind to the operation: the last `__`-separated segment, not the server prefix, because the same npm server is spelled differently in the next setup.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_guard_secrets_read.py: an MCP read of a dotenv is denied under a server prefix the tests do not hardcode; an MCP read of a README stays quiet

tasks.title: A shard rewritten by sed is refused as its Edit already is
tasks.description: The manifest and shard `.json` paths join the shell-write gate's targets. `_config.source_exts` has no `.json`, so the one act SECURITY.md says a subagent is refused - editing its own shard - sails through by `sed -i` while the same file through `Edit` is refused. Recording catches it from the second Bash call on, and recording is not blocking. The allow case that must stay quiet is an unrelated `.json` that is not the manifest or a shard.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_guard_secrets_read.py: sed -i on a phase shard is refused for a subagent; an unrelated .json stays quiet

tasks.title: A tracked journal file that is gone turns verify red
tasks.description: A tracked journal file that is gone is a finding. `journal_files()` lists what is on disk, so truncation is caught and deletion is silent - `verify` reports a clean chain over the files that remain while SECURITY.md says deletion is "deliberately loud rather than silent". Diff `git ls-files` against the listing; tracked-but-gone is the finding. A file that was never tracked stays quiet, and so does a clone that legitimately has none.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__journal_io.py: a committed journal file deleted from the worktree is a finding; an untracked absence is not

tasks.title: An MCP write reaches the plan gate, the journal and the token ban
tasks.description: The WRITE half of the MCP hole. Five hooks gate on fixed tool-name sets, so an MCP write tool escapes the plan gate, the self-edit protection, the token-logging ban and the audit journal alike - and a phase shard written through an MCP write is allowed where the same write by `sed` is now refused. Each hook is a separate guard with its own semantics, so each needs its own decision about which MCP operations count as a write; the read half's design rule holds throughout - bind to the operation and the resolved target, never to the server's name.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_require_plan.py: an MCP write outside the plan is refused; an MCP write inside it is allowed and journaled

tasks.title: The loud fallback covers a broken interpreter and an unset plugin root
tasks.description: The loud fallback covers a found-but-broken interpreter and an unset plugin root. A `python3` shim that exits 1 produces no output and exit 1 - an unhandled hook error, which the fail-mode table grades allow for every blocking guard - so the loud `ask` fires only when `command -v` finds nothing at all. And an unset `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` exits 127 before the launcher can run, which is the failure the launcher's own header says it prevents.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_py_launch.py: an interpreter that exits non-zero produces the loud ask, not silence; an unset plugin root does the same

tasks.title: Every event names the agent, and a guard can say it reached one
tasks.description: Every journal event carries the agent that caused it, and every guard can say whether it reached a subagent. The analysis found that nothing proves a hook runs for the executor - the agent that writes the code - so every SECURITY.md promise about subagents is untested. This repo has since driven the other half and found hooks DO reach subagents; what no guard can still say is WHICH agent it refused, and the one measurement behind the zero-agent_id claim rests on one repo and one log, so it is re-taken here before anything is built on it.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_journal_writes.py: an event caused by a subagent carries its agent id; one caused by the orchestrator says so rather than leaving the field empty
